notes: §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR14 makes the invalid key condition exist (a) under random or dynamic access when the relative key names an existing record, (b) 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally defined boundaries of the file', and (c) when the record number has more significant digits than the relative key. RelativeConnector.Write answers (a) '22' from the store, (c) '24' for a sequential release past the key's digits, (b) '24' through RecordWriteFailed for the physical boundary and, since kb/Work PB5125, '24' for a random or dynamic key below 1 or above HighestRelativeRecordNumber, because the DialectBehavior RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError ('34') is active only from 2014; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite runs INVALID KEY on the class-2 status. Probes at --std 85 (classes e and f; a, b, c and d do not reach a run-time invalid key rule): random keys 999999999999999999, 3000000000 and 0 each run INVALID KEY with 24 and the next WRITE (key 5) succeeds 00 (no sticky permanent error), a duplicate gives 22; dynamic 2147483648 gives 24 and keys 7, 2147483647 and 8 then succeed 00; a WRITE after a failed OPEN I-O (35) gives 48 with neither phrase run. The witness covers (a) and (c) for all three access modes (C10 INVALID KEY 24, A3 and D10 22 with the record area kept), and its output matches its .out. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read DIVERGES, naming kb/Work PB5125 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5125 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-12.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-12-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985 GR14: invalid key when (a) under random or dynamic access the key names an existing record, (b) 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally defined boundaries of the file', (c) the record number has more digits than the relative key. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR33 restates a-c with statuses '22', '24', '24' ('When an attempt is made to write outside the externally defined boundaries of the file'); dropping 'random or dynamic' from (a) changes nothing, since sequential WRITE assigns new numbers. But §2023:14.9.51.4 GR29 takes a random or dynamic WRITE whose relative key 'contains a value that is less than 1 or greater than the highest relative record number permitted for the file' out of the invalid key condition: the WRITE is unsuccessful with status '34', a permanent error. 1985 has no such case and no relative status 34; such a WRITE was an attempt to write beyond the file's boundaries, an invalid key (status 24) that runs the INVALID KEY phrase. Under 2023 the INVALID KEY phrase is not run and the fatal-status rules apply. Different result.
